name: Vermont
$scopeNote: STATE income tax only. Vermont has no local income tax anywhere and no reciprocity agreements with any state (residents working elsewhere claim a return-level credit for taxes paid, 32 V.S.A. sec.5825 -- the same disclosed out-of-scope mechanism as every other state's own credit-for-taxes-paid convention in this project). Vermont's Child Care Contribution (CCC, 0.44% of wages subject to VT withholding) is EMPLOYER-paid only, confirmed directly from GB-1210-2026's own text ('Employers must pay a 0.44% payroll tax') -- context-only, not engine-consumed. Vermont Family and Medical Leave Insurance (VT-FMLI) is confirmed VOLUNTARY for both employers and employees (an insurance marketplace program, not a mandatory payroll tax) -- deliberately NOT modeled as a statePaidLeaveEmployee-style universal rate, since doing so would incorrectly deduct it from every Vermont paycheck when in fact most have no VT-FMLI deduction at all; see knownGaps.
$methodComment: GB-1210-2026's own Percentage Method Withholding Tables (fetched and read directly): subtract a flat per-allowance dollar amount (Form W-4VT Line 5 count x the period's own allowance value) from PER-PERIOD gross wages, then look up the result in one of two published per-period bracket tables (Single or Married) -- the same overall shape as New Jersey's Rate Table method, just 2 schedules instead of 5. Brackets published independently per period (weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/quarterly/annual/daily), not derived by dividing an annual table -- transcribed verbatim rather than algebraically derived, unlike Iowa's simpler flat-rate shape.
exemptPretaxComment: GB-1210-2026 states cafeteria-plan pretax treatment 'as though the employee's partner is a spouse' for civil-union purposes, applying 'the federal rules for the payment' -- confirming Vermont generally follows FEDERAL rules for pretax/cafeteria-plan treatment (the civil-union passage's only point of divergence is WHO counts as a spouse, not WHETHER federal pretax rules apply at all). Same conformity pattern as Michigan/Ohio/Idaho/Connecticut/Iowa in this project, opposite of Pennsylvania's non-conformity.

bracketPerPeriodAllowance.$keyRenamedNote: Renamed from 'vermontWithholding' this session, when Nebraska became a second real user of the exact same bracketPerPeriodAllowance() function — the config now lives under the method-named key both states share, matching this project's convention of naming shared config after the shape, not the state that happened to build it first.

reciprocity.note: Vermont has no income-tax reciprocity agreement with any state -- reciprocalStates deliberately empty (checked, found none), not omitted.

knownGaps: Descriptive notes carried from the 2026 file (reciprocity, local-tax rules, method comments) were checked against the 2025 source for the fields this engine computes from; narrative text that only describes 2026 history should be read as background.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).

nonresidentAllocation.$comment: GB-1210-2026 describes the allocation as hours worked in Vermont over total hours in the pay period, with a worked example. Same arithmetic as Connecticut's, a different definition of the fraction — which is why the basis is recorded rather than the two being treated as one rule.

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset: GB-1210 (effective 2025-01-01): 3.35% / 6.6% / 7.6% / 8.75% above $3,825 single / $11,475 married a year, $5,300 per allowance. Per-period tables are the annual ones divided by the periods (thresholds to the dollar, daily to $0.10; bases to the cent), which reproduces the printed quarterly and daily tables.
